questions.title: GATE CSE 1990 | Question: 3-ix
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The number of ways in which $5\; A's, 5\; B's$ and $5\; C's$ can be arranged in a row is:

  1. $15!/(5!)^{3}$
  2. $15!$
  3. $\left(\frac{15}{5}\right)$
  4. $15!(5!3!)$.

review.independentCheck: The multinomial coefficient counts arrangements of five identical A's, five identical B's, and five identical C's.
review.notes: The multinomial coefficient counts arrangements of five identical A's, five identical B's, and five identical C's.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1990 | Question: 3-x
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Indicate which of the following well-formed formulae are valid:

  1. $\left(P\Rightarrow Q\right) {\wedge} \left(Q \Rightarrow R\right) \Rightarrow \left(P \Rightarrow R\right)$
  2. $\left(P\Rightarrow Q\right) \Rightarrow \left( \neg P \Rightarrow \neg Q\right)$
  3. $\left(P{\wedge} \left(\neg P \vee  \neg Q\right)\right) \Rightarrow Q$
  4. $\left(P \Rightarrow R\right) \vee \left(Q \Rightarrow R\right) \Rightarrow \left(\left(P \vee Q \right)  \Rightarrow R\right)$

review.independentCheck: A is implication transitivity; explicit assignments disprove B, C, and D.
review.notes: A is implication transitivity; explicit assignments disprove B, C, and D.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1990 | Question: 3-xi
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
A graph is planar if and only if,

  1. It does not contain a subgraph homeomorphic to $k_{5}$ and $k_{3, 3}$.
  2. It does not contain a subgraph isomorphic to $k_{5}$ and $k_{3, 3}$.
  3. It does not contain a subgraph isomorphic to $k_{5}$ or $k_{3, 3}$
  4. It does not contain a subgraph homeomorphic to $k_{5}$ or $k_{3, 3}$.

review.independentCheck: Kuratowski's theorem uses a subdivision of K5 or K3,3, matching D.
review.notes: Kuratowski's theorem uses a subdivision of K5 or K3,3, matching D.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1989 | Question: 3-v
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following well-formed formulas are equivalent?

  1. $P \rightarrow Q$
  2. $\neg Q \rightarrow \neg P$
  3. $\neg P \vee Q$
  4. $\neg Q \rightarrow P$

review.independentCheck: A, B, and C are the implication and contrapositive equivalences; D fails at P=true, Q=false.
review.notes: A, B, and C are the implication and contrapositive equivalences; D fails at P=true, Q=false.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1989 | Question: 3-vii
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Answer the following:

Which of the following statements are FALSE?

  1. For poisson distribution, the mean is twice the variance.

  2. In queuing theory, if arrivals occur according to poisson distribution, then the inter-arrival time is exponentially distributed.

  3. The distribution of waiting time is independent of the service discipline used in selecting the waiting customers for service.

  4. If the time between successive arrivals is exponential, then the time between the occurences of every third arrival is also exponential.

review.independentCheck: Independent check finds option D false as well: the sum of three exponential gaps is Erlang, so the existing [A,C] answer conflicts with the stem.
review.notes: The stored MSQ key is [A,C], but option D is also false: the interval spanning every three arrivals is the sum of three independent exponential inter-arrival times, which has an Erlang (Gamma shape 3) distribution, not an exponential distribution. Keep the existing key unchanged and hold this solution until the source key is reconciled.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record and source stem; an independent check found an unresolved stem/key issue.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1987 | Question: 1-xxii
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The equation $7x^{7}+14x^{6}+12x^{5}+3x^{4}+12x^{3}+10x^{2}+5x+7=0$ has

  1. All complex roots
  2. At least one real root
  3. Four pairs of imaginary roots
  4. None of the above

review.independentCheck: A degree-seven real polynomial has a real zero by odd-degree end behavior and continuity; source key B agrees.
review.notes: A degree-seven real polynomial has a real zero by odd-degree end behavior and continuity; source key B agrees.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1987 | Question: 1-xxiii
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
A square matrix is singular whenever 

  1. The rows are linearly independent
  2. The columns are linearly independent
  3. The row are linearly dependent
  4. None of the above

review.independentCheck: A square matrix is singular iff its rows (equivalently columns) are dependent; source key C agrees.
review.notes: A square matrix is singular iff its rows (equivalently columns) are dependent; source key C agrees.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1987 | Question: 1-xxvi
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
If $f(x_{i}).f(x_{i+1})< 0$ then

  1. There must be a root of $f(x)$ between $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$
  2. There need not be a root of $f(x)$ between $x_{i}$ and $x_{i+1}$
  3. There fourth derivative of $f(x)$ with respect to $x$ vanishes at $x_{i}$
  4. The fourth derivative of $f(x)$ with respect to $x$ vanishes at $x_{i+1}$

review.independentCheck: A sign change guarantees a root only with continuity; that hypothesis is absent from the displayed stem.
review.notes: The sign-change theorem requires continuity on the interval. The displayed stem does not state continuity, so the stored Option A is not guaranteed as written; the source discussion also notes A is conditional on continuity. Keep the answer key unchanged and hold this solution pending a stem/source decision.
